description: Visual standards Gemini checks every rendered frame against. Each rule has an ID, a human-readable description, and a machine-readable check specification.

TYP-01.name: single-line-text
TYP-01.description: All on-screen text (headlines, overlays, captions, labels) must fit on a single line. No text element should wrap to a second line. If text is too long, the font must shrink to fit one line.
TYP-01.check: Count distinct lines of visible text in the frame. Headlines/overlays that span more than one line = FAIL.

TYP-02.name: text-contrast
TYP-02.description: Every text element must be clearly readable against its background. Minimum contrast ratio: 4.5:1 for body text, 3:1 for large text (>24px equivalent). White or bright text on dark backgrounds. No low-contrast text.
TYP-02.check: Is every piece of text clearly legible? Could you read it instantly at phone screen size?

TYP-03.name: text-safe-zone
TYP-03.description: No text may appear in the top 15% or bottom 12% of the frame (reserved for platform UI on YouTube Shorts). All text must be within the safe zone.
TYP-03.check: Is any text clipped by or positioned in the platform-reserved zones at top/bottom of frame?

VIS-01.name: visual-audio-alignment
VIS-01.description: The visual content on screen must directly relate to what is being said in the voiceover at that moment. If the voiceover mentions a specific number, that number should be visible. If it mentions a comparison, the visual should show a comparison. The viewer should understand the point even on mute.
VIS-01.check: Given the voiceover text for this moment, does the visual content support, illustrate, or reinforce what is being said? Would the visual make sense without audio?

VIS-02.name: visual-clarity
VIS-02.description: Each frame must have exactly one focal point — the single thing the viewer's eye should go to. No clutter, no competing elements. The focal element must be immediately obvious.
VIS-02.check: Can you identify the ONE thing the viewer should look at? Is there visual clutter or competing elements?

VIS-03.name: no-empty-frames
VIS-03.description: No frame should appear empty, broken, or show only a solid background color with no visual content. Every frame must have meaningful visual content.
VIS-03.check: Is this frame empty or showing only a background? Does it look broken or incomplete?

VIS-04.name: visual-variety
VIS-04.description: Consecutive beats/scenes must look visually distinct from each other. No two adjacent visual segments should use the same layout, the same visual treatment, or appear identical.
VIS-04.check: Does this frame look meaningfully different from the previous beat's frame?

COL-01.name: on-palette
COL-01.description: All colors used must come from the channel's declared palette (primary + secondary colors in visual-identity.json). No off-brand or random colors.
COL-01.check: Are all visible colors consistent with the channel's palette? Any jarring or off-brand colors?

LAY-01.name: breathing-room
LAY-01.description: Visual elements must have adequate spacing from frame edges and from each other. No cramped layouts. Minimum 5% margin from all edges for non-background elements.
LAY-01.check: Do visual elements have breathing room? Is anything cramped against the edge or overlapping other elements?

LAY-02.name: visual-hierarchy
LAY-02.description: The most important element (the number, the comparison, the key word) must be the largest and most prominent thing on screen. Supporting elements must be visually subordinate.
LAY-02.check: Is the most important piece of information the most visually prominent element?

gemini_prompt_template:
You are a visual QA editor reviewing frames from a YouTube Shorts video. You have access to the Visual Bible — a set of standards every frame must meet.

For each frame, you will receive:
1. The frame image
2. The voiceover text being spoken at this moment
3. The beat/scene type and intended visual treatment

Your job: check the frame against each Visual Bible rule and report:
- PASS or FAIL for each rule
- For each FAIL, explain what's wrong and suggest a specific fix
- Rate overall quality 1-10
- One sentence: what would make this frame better?

Be harsh. A frame that merely looks 'okay' is not good enough for retention. Every frame must earn the viewer's next second of attention.

Respond ONLY with JSON:
{
  "frame_index": <int>,
  "checks": {
    "<rule_id>": { "pass": true|false, "note": "<explanation if fail>" }
  },
  "quality_score": <1-10>,
  "improvement": "<one specific actionable suggestion>",
  "visual_audio_match": true|false,
  "visual_audio_note": "<how well the visual matches what is being said>"
}
